title: One Model Family, Two Gold-Level Results: Fine-Tuning Nemotron for IOI and IMO
key_facts: Nvidia says Nemotron models were fine-tuned to reach gold-medal level at the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) 2026 and the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) 2026.
The IMO system scored 30 of 42 points; its submitted proofs were graded by official IMO graders.
The IOI result was an unofficial, unsupervised run under contest-like limits, not in the official IOI ranking; it scored 535.4 out of 600.
The IMO system worked in natural language, with no formal prover, external tools or internet access.
Nvidia released the IMO checkpoints, both training datasets and Nemotron-IMO-Bench, a benchmark of 200 olympiad-level problems.
quote_evidence: It was an unofficial, unsupervised benchmark and was not included in the official IOI ranking.
The IMO system’s submitted proofs were graded by official IMO graders.
The IOI result came from a live, prospective run under the same time, internet-access, and submission constraints as human contestants.
why_it_matters_hint: A specialised version of an existing model reached gold-medal level on hard reasoning tests, but the coding result is unofficial.
event_date: IMO 2026 and IOI 2026 (contest years; exact dates not stated); blog article time 7 Oct 2026
notes: Read from the Hugging Face blog (5,737 chars). All figures are Nvidia's; the IMO grading was official, the IOI run was unofficial.
